name: Shemaah
overview: Shemaah was a male warrior from the tribe of Benjamin known as the Gibeathite. He is noted for coming to David at Ziklag, demonstrating his allegiance during a critical period in David's rise to kingship. His tribal affiliation and unique designation as the Gibeathite identify him within the historical context of Israel's united monarchy.
namesAndTitles: The name Shemaah means 'he has heard' or 'he is obedient,' reflecting a character of attentiveness or submission. This proper name is recorded without indication that it was given directly by God, emphasizing its human origin and common Hebrew roots.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture infers that Shemaah was a descendant of Benjamin and possibly the son of Ahiezer and Joash, linking him to a known family line within the tribe. These relationships help situate him within the genealogical and tribal framework of Israel as recorded in the Chronicles.
scriptureSignificance: Shemaah's significance lies in his support of David during a pivotal moment when David was consolidating his leadership. As a Gibeathite from Benjamin who joined David at Ziklag, he represents the gathering of loyal warriors from diverse tribes, which was essential for David's eventual kingship over Israel. His mention underscores the unity and support David received beyond his own tribe of Judah.
